scope: Plasticity, microplasticity, sheet forming, and strengthening cards: moduleIds lecture-4-microplasticity, lecture-5-strengthening, self-plastic-deformation, self-strengthening, plus visible Plasticity-section cards in the same source/topic scope.
summary: Checked 141 cards against Lecture 4 Microplasticity, Lecture 5 Strengthening of Metals, the strengthening and shaping self-assessment PDFs, Test 2024.12.10, past-exam wording where applicable, and matching notes-split pages. No critical wrong-answer issues found. Most explanations match the course treatment of Schmid law/CRSS, slip systems, grain boundaries, twinning, SFE, work hardening, recovery/recrystallization, Cottrell atmospheres, precipitation/dispersion strengthening, anisotropy, FLD, and hot/cold forming. Two minor reportable issues were found.

issues.problem: The correct answer B is consistent with Schmid law, but option D says "the grains start to shear relatively" in a question explicitly about the CRSS of a single crystal. Since a single crystal has no grains, D is also awkward/potentially misleading unless preserved purely as past-exam wording. The current explanation notes that D is badly phrased but does not make the intended interpretation clear.
issues.sourceEvidence: PAST_EXAMS/QUESTIONS_SET_1.txt, Session of February 26, 2024 Version A, Q2 uses the same awkward option. Lecture 4 Microplasticity (1).pdf, pages/slides 4-6 defines CRSS for slip-system activation in a single crystal through tau_RSS = sigma cos(theta) cos(phi), and does not describe relative shearing of multiple grains for the single-crystal case.
issues.proposedFix: Keep B as correct, but clarify the distractor/explanation: "D preserves the professor's awkward past-exam wording; interpreted as relative shear/slip it is not the intended false clause, but in strict wording a single crystal has no grains. The tested false statement is B because tau_CRSS is related to, not identical with, macroscopic yield stress." Alternatively rephrase D to "the active slip planes start to shear relatively."

issues.problem: The card belongs to moduleId self-strengthening and tests precipitation hardening, but its section is "Al & Casting". This makes a strengthening card less visible in the Plasticity/strengthening topic path, unlike the neighbouring self-strengthening cards.
issues.sourceEvidence: Self-assesment questions/self-assessment questions on Strengthening.pdf, page 4 asks about precipitation strengthening, precipitates at grain boundaries vs inside grains, Orowan interpretation, and precipitation vs dispersion hardening. The card is factually correct for that source, but it is categorized outside the Plasticity section.
issues.proposedFix: If topic grouping is intended to follow the strengthening source, change section to "Plasticity". If the master agent intentionally wants Al precipitation cards under Al & Casting, no factual change is needed.

uncertainties.note: The hot-forging-over-hot-rolling answer is technically sound and fits the self-assessment prompt, but the extracted assigned sources provide the prompt and hot-rolling notes rather than a direct professor-written answer comparing forging and rolling product/property requirements.

The FCC/BCC slip-behavior comparison is consistent with standard course logic and the self-assessment prompt on FCC vs BCC and Peierls-Nabarro stress, but the assigned PDFs I extracted contain the prompt rather than a full worked professor answer for Peierls-Nabarro temperature/strain-rate sensitivity.
